title: Remapping a shortcut allows extra modifier keys

status.label: Reproduce the extra-modifier shortcut match
status.detail: The reporter supplied the exact mapping Win+Right → End and says Ctrl+Win+Right also triggers it, but the mapping was removed and the only reported build is 0.79.0.

judgment.rationale: The issue now contains the exact mapping and trigger sequence: Win+Right maps to End, yet Ctrl+Win+Right reportedly triggers it too. The author removed the mapping because it interfered with the native virtual-desktop shortcut, and the report is on 0.79.0 with no current-build retest. This is a direct maintainer reproduction on a current build; do not infer a fix before verifying exact-modifier matching still fails.
evidence: The issue lists PowerToys 0.79.0 and says Win+Right is mapped to End.
The author clarified that pressing Ctrl+Win+Right also triggers the mapping, although Ctrl was not part of the configured shortcut.
The author removed the mapping because it interfered with the native virtual-desktop shortcut.
A contributor requested the exact target in 2024; the author supplied it. The issue has no assignee.
judgment.recommended_action: Test the exact mapping on PowerToys 0.100.2 or newer and confirm whether the extra Ctrl modifier still triggers the remap.

fix_assessment.rationale: The exact historical behavior is testable, but it is reported only on 0.79.0 and the author removed the mapping. Confirm whether the shortcut matcher still accepts a superset of the configured modifiers on a current build before proposing a correction.

issue_context.summary: Win+Right mapped to End reportedly also triggers when Ctrl is held, overriding Ctrl+Win+Right’s native virtual-desktop behavior.
known_information: The report lists PowerToys 0.79.0 and no administrator elevation.
The author clarified the exact mapping as Win+Right → End and the unexpected trigger as Ctrl+Win+Right.
The author removed the mapping because the behavior was more disruptive than losing that shortcut.
There is no current-build retest or assignee.
inferences: The matcher may be treating a configured shortcut as a subset of a chord with additional modifiers, but the issue does not establish whether the same behavior remains in current code.
issue_context.analysis: The author’s clarification makes this a narrow current-build test rather than a generic shortcut failure. Compare the configured Win+Right with Ctrl+Win+Right and check whether End is emitted or the virtual desktop changes.
initial_investigation: Read the full issue and all four comments, including the author’s exact mapping and reason for removing it.
No later report or current-version confirmation appears in the live thread.

actions.label: Test extra-modifier shortcut matching
actions.note: The exact historical mapping is known; verify whether the behavior remains before proposing a matcher change.

reproduce.title: Verify extra modifiers do not trigger a shortcut remap
prerequisites: Windows desktop with at least two virtual desktops available
setup: Add a shortcut remap with Win+Right as the source and End as the target.
steps: Press Win+Right without Ctrl and verify that End is sent.
Press Ctrl+Win+Right and observe whether End is sent or Windows switches to the next virtual desktop.
Remove the temporary mapping after the test.
reproduce.expected_result: Only the exact configured Win+Right chord should trigger the End remap; adding Ctrl should leave the chord unmapped and preserve the native virtual-desktop shortcut.
